rationale.usefulness: Released data, prompt/configuration scripts and clearly described sensitivity tests give research-app builders and educators an actionable way to question novelty scores. The report preserves human review, distinguishes label accuracy from disagreement and proposes reasonable classroom, website and explainer uses.
rationale.impact: The controlled study addresses an important component of automated research and exposes large same-input verdict reversals. One conference, extreme case selection, weak generated labels and limited configuration interactions bound how far the findings can reshape general AI evaluation practice.
rationale.novelty: A reusable review-mining pipeline and controlled comparison on human versus generated ideas meaningfully extend the study of novelty judges. General judge prompt sensitivity and presentation bias are already established issues, so the new contribution is a focused benchmark and empirical characterization.
rationale.maturity: The paper, public benchmark, scripts and documented aggregation/metric rules support a usable research evaluation artifact. It is not a validated production novelty oracle; generated labels, small expert checks, proprietary model dependence and missing released judge traces constrain reliability and replication.
rationale.openness: Apache-2.0 code, ODC-BY data, explicit OpenReview attribution and visible configuration/reproduction instructions provide substantial transparency. Provider API costs and terms, absent raw judge outputs and limited original annotation validation prevent an exceptional reproducibility rating.

concerns: No publication-blocking factual issue found. The report avoids presenting prompt variants as semantically identical and explicitly qualifies generated labels, single-call retrieval comparisons and unequal aggregation in cost comparisons.

Source limitation: the archived arXiv HTML conversion ends during Appendix A.1.1 and reports conversion errors. Main claims used in the report are supported by visible main text plus the release post/repository/dataset card; the archive should not be treated as a complete appendix or experimental-log record.

The repository README describes 28 difficult pairs plus 2 controls while the paper main text describes 25 plus 5. The report safely states 30 pairs concentrated on difficult errors without asserting either inconsistent split.
